messages:
Sophie: FYI customer ACME just opened a ticket — invoice shows ~1.2M embedding units for Feb but dashboard usage is ~850k. They only use the embeddings/rerank flows in batched requests. Can someone triage?

Ryan: on it. Can you attach the invoice line item + an example request payload? Also which model/endpoint?

Sophie: Invoice snippet: INV-2025-3421 line item: embedding.unit 1,203,412 @ 0.0004. Dashboard: embed_units=852,110 for same billing period. Customer says they use batch size 10 mostly, occasionally 50. Endpoint: /v1/embeddings (model: open-embed-1) then a rerank step. Example request they sent (redacted):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["","short note","very long text...","   ","another short"],"truncate":"end","max_tokens":128}'

Ingrid: hmm empty strings + whitespace-only inputs in the batch can be tricky. I remember a runtime edge where truncated/empty inputs were still counted in pairwise rerank accounting if we later ran rerank logic on the batch.

Alex: I ran a quick repro locally with a 5-item batch that included empty/whitespace-only inputs. Repro steps: send the exact payload above then follow with the customer's rerank call (they do server-side pairwise scoring). Logs show two meter events per request: one embedding.batch with units=5 and one rerank.pairwise with units=10 (n*(n-1)/2). But the dashboard only surfaces embedding.batch events; invoices include both embedding and pairwise meter entries.

Log snippet: 
[2025-03-12T14:02:01Z] request_id=r-abc123 event=embedding.batch inputs=5 charged_units=5 model=open-embed-1
[2025-03-12T14:02:01Z] request_id=r-abc123 event=rerank.pairwise pairs=10 charged_units=10 note=includes_empty_inputs=true

BillingBot: I looked up the invoice line: it contains two meter_types for that customer within the same window: "embedding.unit" and "rerank.pairwise"; usage timestamps line up with the customer's batch traffic pattern. There are ~350k pairwise units billed that are absent from the dashboard aggregates because the UI aggregates only embedding.unit by default.

Maria: Root cause hypothesis: when an input tokenizes to zero tokens (empty or whitespace after truncate), the embedding code still increments the batch count (so embedding.units includes them) and the rerank path later computes pairwise counts using n=total batch size rather than n=non-empty vectors. That double-counts logical work and leads to higher invoice totals.

Alex: Confirmed — runtime produced a zero-dim vector placeholder for empty inputs and still enqueued them for pairwise scoring. The pairwise meter used batch length before filtering, so charged pairs = n*(n-1)/2 even if some vectors were zeroed. Patch idea: short-circuit pairwise meter when vector_dim == 0 or pre-filter empty inputs before pair counting.

BillingOps: For mitigation we need to calculate credits. Please export all pairwise meter events for that account between 2025-02-01 and 2025-02-28 and flag those where payloads had empty_input_count > 0. We can then compute overcharge = sum(pairwise_charged_units where should_have_been_filtered).

Sophie: Customer already provided a replay CSV of their requests. I'll share it with BillingOps and attach to the ticket. They want a timeframe and rough credit estimate before EOD.

Maria: Hotfix plan: 1) immediate check in runtime to skip emitting rerank.pairwise meter when input vector dims are zero (hotfix, ~2-3 hours deploy), 2) subsequent fix to pre-filter empty inputs earlier in pipeline + add a dashboard tile for pairwise meters (to make invoices match UI), 3) backfill credits for affected accounts.

Alex: I pushed a small guard: if embed_vector_dim == 0 then do not increment rerank.pairwise meter. Running integration tests now. If green I'll cut a canary to staging and then prod.

BillingOps: Once you have the list of affected request_ids/usage events tag them and I'll run the credit calculation. We need to provide the customer with the credit delta and a short explanation.

Sophie: Thanks team. I'll keep ACME updated. ETA for hotfix to customer message: ~3h. Will follow up with credit numbers when BillingOps has the export.

Ryan: Adding a short-term support note: advise customers to trim whitespace and filter empty inputs client-side. We'll follow up with an SDK patch that warns on empty inputs for batched embeddings.

Sophie: Marking P1 (billing) and linking ticket #SUP-4022.
